results.title: [PDF] Full Employment: A Survey of Theory, Empirics and Policies
results.content: 28 FULL EMPLOYMENT POLICY PROGRAMS Working Paper 249 Table 2 / Continued Country Program Timeframe Main Points (3) Public employment guarantee experiment (ensuring all long term unemployed have access to employment) France Territoires zéro chômeur de longue durée (TZCLD) From 2016 › 58 municipalities involved as of 2023 with 1500 placements (< 0.00% of labour force) and funding of 34 million EUR (< 0.00% of GDP) › ‘Job-Oriented Companies’ that hire long-term unemployed for positions that do not crowd out regular private firms Austria Modellprojekt Arbeitsplatzgarantie Marienthal (MAGMA) 2020-2024 › Job guarantee for all long-term unemployed with 250 3-year positions (< 0.00% of labour force) and a program budget of EUR 7.5 million (< 0.02% of GDP) › Focus on one municipality(Gramatneusiedl) › Wages at least at the level of the collectively bargained minimal wage › Regular labour market or social employment, with positions tailored to one’s skillset › evaluation findings available (4) Public employment enforcement USSR Constitutional Duty to Work 1917-1991 › Every able-bodied citizen is by law obliged to work › Full employment is a result of the socialist organisation of economy › Unemployment officially declared non-existent at the end of the 1930s (hidden unemployment) › A political program rather than a specific single policy › Data availability issues, difficult to estimate the true scope Belarus Parasite Tax 2015-2018 › Only-sticks approach, with no active job promotion or creation by the state › Unclear policy goal: increased employment or ‘windfall’ tax revenues?
